* * * *
 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under the provisions of Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ for the death of Shivashankarappa caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioners case are as under:
SCCH - 26 3 MVC No.3725/2021 It is the case of the petitioners that on 13.04.2021 at about 6.15 p.m, Sri.Shivashankarappa (hereinafter referred to as deceased) was proceeding in a Motor Cycle bearing reg.No.KA 40EA3179 along with his friend on Bangalore Hyderabad road and when they reached near Bandahalli Cross, NH - 48 road, Chikkaballapura Taluk and District, at that time,
a Ashoka Leyland Lorry bearing reg.No.TN81A2496 being driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner came and dashed against the Motor Cycle of the deceased.
Due to impact the deceased fell on the ground and sustained grievous injuries all over his body and died on the spot.
Thereafter, the post mortem was conducted at Government Hospital, Chikkaballapura on the body of the deceased and handed over the same to them.
They conducted the funeral and other ceremonies by spending a sum of Rs.1,00,000/ towards funeral charges.

3. Further it is the case of the Petitioners that prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy and was doing Coolie and earning Rs.20,000/ per month and was contributing same to the family maintenance.

Due to his death, petitioners lost beloved SCCH - 26 4 MVC No.3725/2021 husband,
father and son respectively and earning member of the family.

The accident occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry and in this regard FIR came to be registered in crime No.68/2021 for the offences punishable under Section 279, 304(a) of IPC at Gudibande police Smt. Gangarathna vs R Chinnaswamy on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174799723/
2 station.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, they have prayed to award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ from the respondents.
4. The notice of the petition has been duly served on Respondent No.1 and 2.
The Respondent No.1 has not appeared before this Tribunal.
Hence, Respondent No.1 has been placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 has appeared before this tribunal and filed his written statement.
The Respondent No.2 has denied the entire petition averments as false and baseless.
Further he has contended that the driver of the lorry was not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of alleged accident.
Further he has contended that the petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary party.
He has also contended that the owner of the offending vehicle and the deceased were not having valid driving licence and SCCH - 26 5 MVC No.3725/2021 other documents like RC, FC and permit.
Further he has contended that if any compensation is awarded, the rate of interest may be restricted to 6% p.a.
With these contentions he has prayed to reject the claim petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings of both the parties, the following issues have been framed :
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Shivashankarappa ?

2. Whether the Petitioners' prove that, on 13042021 at about 06.15 p.m. the deceased was proceeding on motor cycle bearing KA40EA3179 with his friend towards Bangalore road to Hyderabad road and when he reached near Bandahalli Cross, Chikkaballapur taluk, a lorry bearing Reg. No.TN81A2496 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed his motor cycle from the back side as a result the deceased Shivashankrappa fell on the ground and sustained injuries at his head, legs and all over body and died at the spot, as mentioned in claim petition?
3. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so,
from which respondent?
4.
What Order or Award?
6. The Petitioner No.1 has got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 14 documents as Ex's.P1 to 14.
On the other hand, the SCCH - 26 6 MVC No.3725/2021 respondent No.2 has not chosen to lead its evidence.
7. Heard the arguments from both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. My answers to the above issues are as follows :

3 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly Affirmative Issue No.4 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1:
As already stated supra the Petitioner No.1 has examined herself as PW.1.
she has reiterated petition averments in her affidavit filed for her chief examination.
She has deposed that she is the wife of deceased Shivashankarappa and Petitioner No.2 and 3 are her minor daughters.
Further she has deposed that Petitioner No.4 is the father and Petitioner No.5 is the mother of deceased Shivashankarappa.

In this regard she has produced notarised copy of Aadhar cards of herself and petitioner No.3 at Ex.P.8 and 9, birth certificate of petitioner No.2 at Ex.P.10, ration card at Ex.P.11, election identity card of deceased at Ex.P.12 SCCH - 26 7 MVC No.3725/2021 and Aadhar cards of petitioner No.4 and 5 at Ex.P.13 and 14.
As per these documents it is clear that Petitioner No.1 is wife of deceased, Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the daughters of the deceased and Petitioner No.4 and 5 are the parents of the deceased.
Though the learned counsel for the Respondent No.2 has cross examined PW.1 but he has not failed to elicit anything from PW.1 to disbelieve their relationship with the deceased.
Therefore, this tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioners No.1 to 5 are the legal heirs of deceased.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
10. ISSUE NO.2:

PW.1 has stated that on 13.04.2021 at about 6.15 pm., her husband deceased Shivashankarappa was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA40EA3179 along with his friend on Bangalore - Hyderabad road and when they reached near Bandhalli cross, NH48 road,
Chikkaballapur taluk, at that time, a Ashoka Leyland Lorry bearing reg.No.TN81A2496 being driven by its driver at high speed and in a rash and negligent manner came and dashed against the Motor Cycle of the deceased as a result, the deceased fell on the ground and sustained injuries and died at the spot.

Further she has deposed that the accident SCCH - 26 8 MVC No.3725/2021 occurred only due to negligence on the part of driver of the lorry and in this regard FIR in Crime No.68/2021came to be registered at Gudibande police station against the driver of the lorry for the offences punishable under Section 279, 304(A) of IPC.

In support of her evidence she has produced true copy of FIR, compliant, spot panchanama, rough sketch, inquest panchanama, PM report and charge sheet which are marked at Ex.P.1 to 7.
11.

From the evidence on record it can be seen that after receipt of complaint lodged by one Satish,
the Gudibande police have registered FIR in Crime No.68/2021 against the driver of lorry bearing reg.No.TN81A2496 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 304(A) of IPC.
After due investigation the police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending lorry for the offences punishable u/s 279, 304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P.4 is the rough sketch which shows that the accident took place at NH  44 BangaloreHyderabad road on the extreme left side.
Further it appears that both the vehicles were proceeding towards same direction.
The IMV report placed on record shows that the accident occurred not due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.
Ex.P.5 is the inquest report and SCCH - 26 9 MVC No.3725/2021 Ex.P.6 is the PM report of deceased.
As per these documents the deceased died due to head shock and heamorrhage as a result of multiple injuries sustained in road traffic accident.

Though the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has cross examined PW1 Smt. Gangarathna vs R Chinnaswamy on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174799723/
4 but he has failed to elicit anything from her to disbelieve her version.

sentences.text: Further she has clearly denied the suggestion that due to the negligence on the part of the deceased, the accident had occurred.
Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the chargesheet filed by the police is collusive or defective.
12. On the other hand the Respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence in support of his contentions.

Therefore, from the evidence adduced by the Petitioners it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending lorry bearing reg.No.TN81A2496.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence"
has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compared to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the chapter in M.V.Act dealing with compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore, based on the SCCH - 26 10 MVC No.3725/2021 above discussion, I hold that the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry bearing reg.No.TN81A2496 is proved.
As such, I answer issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
13. ISSUE NO.3:
As per the documents produced by the PW.1 it is clear that Petitioner No.1 to 5 are the dependants on the income of deceased.
As such, Petitioner No.1 to 5 are entitled for compensation under the head loss of dependency.
14. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY: PW.1 has produced the notarized copy of Election Identity card of deceased at Ex.P.12.
But this document does not disclose the exact date of birth of the deceased.
However, this document shows the birth of year of deceased as 1972.
As per PM report marked at Ex.P.6 the age of the deceased is shown as 42 years.
Hence, it indicates that the deceased was aged about 42 years.

Therefore, the appropriate multiplier as per Sarala Verma's case for the said age group is "14".
15.
According to PW.1 her deceased husband was doing coolie and earning Rs.20,000/ p.m.
To prove the same PW.1 has SCCH - 26 11 MVC No.3725/2021 not produced any document.
Even she has not adduced any witnesses to show the income and avocation of the deceased.
In the absence of proof of avocation and income, this tribunal has to consider notional income for calculating the compensation.
As per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Service Authority the notional income of the deceased is taken as Rs.15,000/ as the accident took place in the year 2021.
16. In the present case the deceased was aged about 42 years.
His notional income is taken as Rs.15,000/ p.m.

As per the Hon'ble Apex court reported in a decision reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court cases 680 (National Insurance company Ltd., Vs Pranay Sethi and others), 25% of income is to be added towards future prospects as the deceased was self employed.

sentences.text:
Therefore, 25%
of Rs.15,000/ works out to Rs.3,750/.
Therefore the total income of the deceased works out to Rs.18,750/ (Rs.15,000/ + Rs.3,750/).
Since the petitioner No.1 to 5 are the dependents of the deceased, the 1/4th of the total salary is to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
Hence, 1/4th of Rs.18,750/ works out to Rs.4,688/.

Income for consideration is Rs.14,062/ (18,750/ ()

5 4,688/).
Annual income works out to Rs.1,68,744/ (14,062/ x SCCH - 26 12 MVC No.3725/2021 12).
Appropriate multiplier is "14".
Thus loss of dependency worksout to Rs.23,62,416/ (1,68,744 x 14).
17. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

It is relevant to note that due to the death of deceased, petitioner No.1 lost her beloved husband and petitioner No.2 and 3 lost their beloved father and they have also lost their parental aid, protection, affection, discipline, guidance and training.
Similarly, petitioner No.4 and 5 have lost their beloved son.

Therefore, in view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court in civil Appeal No.2705/2020 in the case of United India Insurance company Ltd., Vs Satinder Kaur and others, each of the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/ on account of loss of consortium and loss of love and affection.

sentences.text:
18. LOSS OF ESTATE: Petitioners are entitled for Rs.15,000/ towards loss of estate.
19.
FUNERAL EXPENSES:

Petitioners are entitled for Rs.15,000/ towards funeral expenses.
20.

The calculation table stands as follows : 1 Loss of dependency Rs. 23,62,416 =00 SCCH - 26 13 MVC No.3725/2021 2 Loss of consortium Rs. 2,00,000=00 (Petitioner No.1 to 5) 3 Loss of estate Rs. 15,000=00 4
Funeral expenses Rs. 15,000=00
GRAND TOTAL Rs.25,92,416=00
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.25,92,416/.
21. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.

22. The respondent No.1 is the RC owner of offending lorry and respondent No.2 is insurer of the said lorry and it is admitted fact that as on the date of the accident, the offending Lorry was having valid insurance policy.

Therefore respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of SCCH - 26 14 MVC No.3725/2021 this order.

Accordingly, I answer issue No.3 'in the Partly affirmative'.
23. ISSUE NO.4 : In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
: ORDER : The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,92,416/ (Rupees Twenty Five Lakhs Ninety Two Thousand Four Hundred and Sixteen only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Smt. Gangarathna vs R Chinnaswamy on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174799723/
6
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1  50% Petitioner No.2 & 3  15% each Petitioner No.4 & 5  10% each SCCH - 26 15 MVC No.3725/2021 Out of the share amount of petitioner No.1, a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to her on proper verification.
However the said petitioner No.1 at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
Since the the petitioner No.2 and 3 are minors, their share amount shall be deposited in any nationalised/scheduled bank as a fixed deposits in their names till they attain the age of majority.
The entire share amount of petitioner No.4 and 5 shall be released in their favour through E Payment after proper verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw an award accordingly.
